scientific-calculator.formula:
Order of operations (PEMDAS/BODMAS):
1. Parentheses and functions: sin, cos, tan, ln, log, √
2. Powers: xʸ (right-associative: 2^3^2 = 2^(3^2))
3. Multiplication and division: ×, ÷
4. Addition and subtraction: +, −

Factorial: n! = 1 × 2 × ... × n  (whole numbers 0–170)
howTo: Tap the digit and operator keys to build your expression — it appears live above the result.
Use ( and ) to group parts of the expression; you can nest them.
Tap a function key (sin, cos, ln, √, ...) then type the value and close the parenthesis.
Switch between DEG and RAD above the display before doing trigonometry.
Press = to evaluate. Tap any history entry to reuse that calculation.
keyFacts: The calculator evaluates expressions with correct order of operations — 2+3×4 gives 14, not 20.
Trigonometric functions work in both degrees and radians; DEG is the default.
Implicit multiplication is supported: 2(3+4), 2π and 3(2)^2 all evaluate correctly.
The Ans key inserts the previous answer so you can chain calculations without retyping.
scientific-calculator.keywords: scientific calculator, online calculator, trigonometry calculator, log calculator, factorial calculator
limitations: Results are limited by double-precision floating point — e.g. 0.1+0.2 shows as 0.30000000000000004 before display rounding.
Factorials only work for whole numbers 0–170; larger values overflow.
Very large or tiny results may display in rounded form; up to 10 significant digits are shown.
This is a calculator, not a symbolic algebra system — it cannot solve equations or simplify expressions.
